0.value:
pc_background learns the empty room, then removes it from every cloud after.

THE CLOUD FRAME, AND WHY pc_crop GOES FIRST:
A cloud travelling between these nodes is either a plain (N, 3) array of points, or a small dict carrying the points AND the volume they were cropped to.

pc_crop is what turns the first into the second. Every grid-based node downstream then uses the volume carried on the frame to build its voxel grid, and their own min/max widgets are only a fallback for when a raw array arrives with nothing attached.

So pc_crop belongs at the head of the chain, and not only to throw away points. It is how the rest of the chain learns what volume it is working in. Set the box once, at the top, and everything after it agrees.

The metadata is passed along by every node, and the renderers unwrap it, so either form draws directly - you never have to unpack it by hand.

SHOW IT THE EMPTY ROOM:
Press 'learn' with nobody in the volume. It watches for 'frames' frames, marks every voxel that was occupied in at least 'min hits' of them, and from then on throws away any point landing in one of those voxels. While it is learning it passes the whole scene through unchanged.

What is left is whatever is NEW - which for most installations is the person. It is far more robust than trying to crop a person out geometrically, because it does not care what shape the room is.

PRESS learn WITH THE CLOUD ALREADY RUNNING:
This is the one procedural trap. The learned model is tied to the exact voxel grid it was built on, so if the volume changes - because the first frame arrives carrying a crop, or because you adjust the crop or the voxel size - the model no longer maps to anything and is thrown away.

Start the sensor, get the crop the way you want it, and only then press learn. Done the other way round, the node prints in the console that it has abandoned the run, and you press learn again.

'dilate' IS USUALLY WORTH 1:
Sensor noise makes points on a learned surface jitter into neighbouring voxels, where the model does not expect them, and they survive as a thin crust of false foreground. dilate grows the background by that many voxels to catch them.

Measured on a 3,000-point wall jittering by 2 cm, with 5 cm voxels:

dilate 0     37 points of wall survive
dilate 1      0 points survive

and a 1,500-point person in front of the wall was untouched at every setting. The cost of dilating is that the background grows slightly, so something pressed right up against a learned surface starts to disappear into it. The node starts at 0; 1 is the sensible setting, and higher only if the crust persists. dilate is applied when learning finishes, so change it before pressing learn.

'clear' throws the model away and passes everything through again.

THE GRID:
'voxel size (cm)' is the resolution of the model, 5 cm by default. If an upstream pc_voxel has put its voxel size on the frame, that is used instead. The volume is the crop carried on the frame, or else the 'min (x,y,z)' and 'max (x,y,z)' options (-3 -3 0 to 3 3 6). Points outside the volume pass through untouched.

SYNTAX:
pc_background

EXAMPLE:
pc_background

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

point cloud:
The cloud. Receiving it does the work.

voxel size (cm):
The model's resolution.

learn / frames / min hits:
Start learning, over how many frames (60), requiring how many hits per voxel (20).

dilate (voxels):
Grow the learned background to catch surface jitter. 1 is usually right.

clear:
Forget the background.

min (x,y,z) / max (x,y,z) (options):
The volume, used only when the frame carries no crop.

OUTPUTS:

foreground:
What was not in the learned background.

RELATED:
pc_crop, which should come before it. pc_denoise for speckle and flicker, which used to share this page. pc_info to see how many points you are actually losing.
